In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of logic programming for large scale knowledge representation in law.
the development and application of logic programming techniques to the representation and manipulation of legal knowledge.

the development and use of a formalism for representing legal knowledge in a way which is sufficiently expressive and flexible to support the kinds of reasoning required for the application of the law in practice.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we are developing a system which can support the legal reasoning of a lawyer in the following tasks: (1) to understand a particular legal problem, (2) to find a relevant piece of legislation, (3) to understand that legislation, (4) to apply that legislation to that particular legal problem, and (5) to present the result of the application.

the project aims to produce a system which can be used to provide advice to a social security office on the entitlement to supplementary benefit of an applicant for benefit; to assist the office in the preparation of benefit awards; and, to provide an on-line reference source for staff of the Department of Social Security.

we are using logic programming to represent and manipulate the knowledge of a legal domain, to support the reasoning tasks of a legal expert system, and to support the construction of a legal expert sytem itself.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of logic for the representation and processing of legal knowledge is feasible and that it can be used to provide a basis for the development of legal information systems.
the use of logic programming in the representation of legal rules is a powerful tool, but one that needs careful application if it is to be used effectively.
logic programming can be used to represent large bodies of legal knowledge in a way which supports the kinds of legal reasoning tasks which are of interest in legal practice.
